algorithm: Greedy binary splits maximizing Gini impurity gain

classes.desc: Binary decision tree grown with greedy Gini-impurity splits.
classes.name: DecisionTree

complexity: O(d * n^2) worst case to find splits for d features, n rows
data_flow_ascii:
--seed -> generate_dataset -> 70/30 split
train -> DecisionTree.fit (recursive Gini splits)
test -> DecisionTree.predict -> accuracy
print_tree renders the learned tree as text
description_sentence: Grows a Gini-based decision tree on seeded synthetic features, prints the tree as text, and reports test accuracy.
failure_note: Pure nodes, max depth, and unsplittable data all terminate as leaf nodes with the majority class, so training always finishes.

functions.desc: Gini impurity of a label list.
functions.name: gini

functions.desc: Generate 2-feature topic rows with binary labels.
functions.name: generate_dataset

functions.desc: Grow the tree from training features X and labels y.
functions.name: DecisionTree.fit

functions.desc: Predict labels for feature vectors X.
functions.name: DecisionTree.predict

functions.desc: Print the tree structure as indented text.
functions.name: print_tree

functions.desc: Parse args, train, print the tree, and report accuracy.
functions.name: main

label: Decision tree classifier
output_shape: An indented text rendering of the learned tree followed by the test accuracy line.
pitch_sentence: A {topic} decision tree in pure Python that learns greedy Gini splits from seeded data and shows its reasoning as a printable tree.

qa.a: The best (feature, threshold) pair is the one maximizing impurity gain, evaluated exhaustively over observed feature values.
--max-depth caps recursion; pure or unsplittable nodes also stop early as majority-class leaves.
qa.q: What stops the tree from growing forever?

qa.a: print_tree walks the nested dict nodes and indents each level, so the whole model is human-readable.

resume_bullet_template: Built a {topic} decision tree classifier in pure Python using greedy Gini-impurity splits; demo prints the learned tree as text and reports test accuracy on a held-out split.
scaling_note: Exhaustive split search is O(n^2)-ish per level, so the demo stays at a few hundred rows; larger data needs histogram or approximate splits.
storage_note: In-memory only: the dataset and the learned tree exist for the run and are not persisted.
tradeoff_note: Exhaustive Gini splits are exact and easy to follow but slow on larger data compared to approximate split finders.
